advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether `python -m rebar.<module>` gate steps (Public-types/Criteria-routing/Security-rules) are in-scope for the ee2a skew convention; if so, extend detection beyond `scripts/*.py` and guard them, else document the scripts/-only scope boundary.
evidence: _build-and-test.yml:545: `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types` (Public-types drift gate, unguarded, in the same patchset-lane `test` job)

The ee2a note quoted in _build-and-test.yml:152-158 says 'a gate step that runs a repo script must skip ... when the script is absent' — module invocations of repo code arguably qualify, but the ticket 1909 AC enumerated only scripts/ steps, so this may be a deliberate scope boundary.
advisory.finding: The structural sweep and the guard convention only cover `scripts/*.py` invocations (via `_SCRIPT_RE = re.compile(r"scripts/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.py")`); gate steps that run repo code via `python -m rebar.<module>` (e.g. Public-types drift `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types`, Criteria-routing parity, Security-rules freshness) run against the checked-out `src/rebar` tree and are subject to the identical definition-vs-tree skew, yet are neither guarded nor detected by the new structural test nor covered behaviorally.
scenarios: An open Gerrit change whose base predates the addition of src/rebar/schemas/gen_types.py runs the Verified lane, which takes the workflow definition from main; `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types` fails with ModuleNotFoundError (exit 1) — the same false Verified -1 class this ticket fixes for scripts/.
